findings.criterion: 1 — resident can share a usable QR pass
findings.issue: The new tests execute mocked Web Share payloads and mount GuestPass directly, but do not open /pass through App/AppProvider, decode the rendered guest-page QR, or complete lookup and redemption; no mobile browser execution is recorded.
findings.consequence: The resident-to-guest artifact remains unverified at the unauthenticated routing, QR rendering/decoding, and gate-redemption integration points.
findings.correction: Run a mobile browser story that generates/shares a live pass, opens the emitted fragment URL unauthenticated, decodes/scans the displayed QR to the exact token, and completes /v1/passes/lookup plus /v1/passes/redeem.

findings.criterion: 2 plus accessibility/security — pass scan prepopulates a verifiable check-in and submits safely
findings.issue: The rendered test types a token with camera disabled and mounts only CheckInCapture. It does not execute QrScanner, route to CheckInConfirm, edit/remove/replace, assert the redeem payload rather than a walk-in request, or render a rejection that arrives after camera navigation.
findings.consequence: The required scan-to-prepopulated-form-to-verified-redemption flow and its post-navigation rejection guard remain unverified in the actual routed screens.
findings.correction: Mount the nested capture/confirm routes with a mocked scanner and deferred lookup or run a browser story; cover hinted/no-hint scans, focus, edit/remove/replace, rejection after navigation, blocked /v1/sessions before acknowledgment, and final /v1/passes/redeem with the intended token and edited plate.

findings.criterion: 3 and 4 — camera scanning fills check-in and checkout plate fields
findings.issue: The iteration explicitly did not run the existing fake-camera check-in story, the new component test disables camera rendering, and no fake-camera checkout story exists.
findings.consequence: Neither camera acceptance criterion is verified through getUserMedia/model decoding and the responsive React UI; checkout has no end-to-end camera evidence.
findings.correction: Run and record e2e/live-plate.mjs at 390x844 with its model/fixture, then add and run a checkout fake-camera story that scans a known open-session plate, asserts the visible field and correct match without manual input, and records browser/model/fixture and console results.

findings.criterion: 5 authorization/UX — configurable overstay policy editor persistence
findings.issue: The rendered test proves the PATCH body and supervisor read-only gate, but its policy data is fixed and reload is a no-op, so it never observes the saved per-tenant value rehydrate after reload. API persistence is tested separately, not through the Settings data flow.
findings.consequence: A broken Settings reload/rehydration boundary could leave an administrator seeing stale policy data despite a successful save.
findings.correction: Use a stateful rendered API mock or browser test that persists the PATCH, returns the updated policy on reload/remount, and asserts 6000 is displayed; retain the supervisor case and assert all editable controls are disabled with no PATCH.

findings.criterion: 6 and 7 plus responsive authorization — Admin CRUD and Super Admin cross-property operations
findings.issue: No iteration-7 test covers these criteria and the record explicitly says the browser stories were not run. Existing CRUD is desktop-only, Super Admin switches properties without representative entity mutation there, and no rendered story proves a regular admin is denied the second property.
findings.consequence: UI CRUD completeness, mobile usability, cross-property Super Admin mutation, and the regular-admin property boundary remain unverified together through the real UI/API path.
findings.correction: Run the existing stories; add person/site/unit/slot create-edit-delete coverage at a narrow mobile viewport, mutate representative entities after a Super Admin switches property, and assert a regular administrator cannot read or mutate that property's entities.
